source.title: LLM-assisted Concept Discovery: Automatically Identifying and Explaining Neuron Functions
source.authors: N. Hoang-Xuan; Minh N. Vu; My T. Thai

page_placements.theme: Measured interpretability depends on the labelling tool, metric, threshold, concept vocabulary, probing data and explainer

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates visual-neuron explanations with a different method and reports comparisons of explanation interpretability and a score based on activations on generated examples and non-examples.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own ResNet50 comparison and CLIP-ResNet50 concept-validation results. The language-model neuron studies in the references are citations, not results from this study. Results said to be in supplementary materials are not present in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: This paper proposes a vision-neuron explanation method (GPT-4V concept discovery plus validation on generated images). Its results are its own method's performance against FALCON and MILAN. It does not measure what share of neurons in a model have one main job, so it neither tests nor uses the claim. The 99/100 versus 11/100 result counts final-layer ResNet50 units that each method managed to label. Those units are ImageNet class outputs, whose concept the task already fixes. That is a tool comparison, not a measure of how clean the neurons are, and not a test of V4's causal account (architecture, regularization, tools). The CLIP validation scores concern a vision model and generated images, not simulated activations on new text, and the paper reports them only as a figure. It cites Bills et al. only in passing.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors conclude that their LLM-assisted discovery yields more insightful, distinctive concepts than FALCON and MILAN. They also conclude that their generated-example and co-hyponym validation score helps users judge concept quality without ground truth.
record.recipe_differences: This is a visual-neuron concept-discovery method using filtered image exemplars, GPT-4V explanations, and generated concept/co-hyponym images for validation; it is not the Qwen neuron-pole audit or the language-model explanation-scoring method in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: For the ResNet50 final-layer interpretability count, the reported share differs between the paper's method and FALCON.

fits_no_version.finding: With GPT-4V-based concept discovery, 99 of the first 100 ResNet50 final-layer class units got an interpretable label, against 11 with FALCON.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Better automated explanation tools label far more vision units than earlier tools, measured on output-class units whose concept is known.

fits_no_version.finding: For 512 last-backbone-layer CLIP-ResNet50 neurons, scores comparing activations on generated concept images versus co-hyponym images are shown only as a distribution. All zero scores come from GPT-4V refusals.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a vision model, many neuron concepts proposed by a multimodal model separate generated examples from near-miss non-examples. The share is not quantified in the text.

record.problems: The explanations are evaluated using generated images and generated co-hyponyms rather than a ground-truth concept set. The supplied text gives one explicit validation score and a figure-only score distribution, with no numerical summary of that distribution.

untested.parts: All: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole shares are not measured.
All: no language models, mixture-of-experts models or scaling are tested.
All: InceptionV1 cat-and-car and pose/recursive generalization are not examined.

There is no test of architecture or regularization as causes, no InceptionV1 estimates, and no validated interpretable share of hidden neurons across tools. The only tool comparison uses final-layer class units.
All: no attribution graphs or circuits.

There is no comparison of explanations that fit activating examples with prediction of where the neuron fires in held-out data for language models. The vision validation scores are reported only as a figure.
There is no simulation-based scoring of language-model neuron explanations and no reported share of well-scored neurons.

record.verdict_notes: The user study, layer experiments and ablations are said to be in supplementary material that is not in the supplied text. The MILAN comparison (168/512 neurons labelled 'text') is likewise a method comparison and is not needed as a row. The reader's V4 'supports' label is removed: comparing tools on class-output units does not bear on how clean hidden neurons are.

versions.untested_parts: The Qwen3-32B neuron-pole shares are not measured.
The paper does not test language models, dense versus mixture-of-experts models, or scaling to larger language models.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car example and the proposed pose or recursive-generalization interpretation are not examined.
The paper compares explanation methods on ResNet50, but does not test architecture or regularization as causes, the InceptionV1 estimates, or how interpretability changes across architectures.
The paper does not build attribution graphs or test whether model neurons suffice as circuit units.

It evaluates visual-neuron concepts on generated images, not language-model explanations on new text, and does not directly compare explanations that fit their original activating examples against predictions on held-out text.
The paper does not score language-model neuron explanations on new text or report the share of explanations achieving good scores.

relation.reason: The 2024 paper predates the original essay and neither tests nor uses the claim. It only mentions polysemanticity as a reason for its exemplar filter. cites_only is the catalog's no-test bucket, and discusses would also be defensible.

tranche.reason: Proposes its own vision-neuron explanation method (GPT-4V discovery, generated-image validation) and reports it against FALCON and MILAN. It measures no share of single-job neurons, so it neither tests nor uses the claim.

source_check.notes: The 99/100 vs 11/100 counts are for ImageNet ResNet50 final-layer class units, which are labelled by the task. FALCON by design labels only units it deems interpretable, so the gap compares methods and says nothing about a share of clean neurons. Figure 6 (512 CLIP-ResNet50 last-layer units) gives only a score distribution with no stated share, and its zero scores are GPT-4V refusals.
